target.title: fix(ios): cancel queued push-to-talk invokes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`ptt_once` bypassed the app's serialized talk-invoke gate, while queued `ptt_start`/`ptt_stop` requests waited in a cancellation-unaware FIFO. If the Gateway timed out a queued request, it could remain in that FIFO and later acquire the microphone, creating a stale push-to-talk capture after its request had ended.

## Why This Change Was Made

All talk commands, including `ptt_once`, now acquire the same gate. Waiters carry stable identities so cancellation removes and resumes only the cancelled waiter without releasing the active owner. A waiter that is resumed after cancellation cannot accidentally transfer the lock. A running one-shot PTT now routes task cancellation through the existing `cancelPushToTalk()` cleanup path.

The i18n inventory changes are source-line updates only.

## User Impact

Overlapping, cancelled, or timed-out PTT commands no longer start a delayed microphone capture. One-shot PTT cannot race normal start/stop PTT commands, and Voice Wake lease cleanup stays paired with the actual capture owner.

## Evidence

- Ran `pnpm native:i18n:check`; inventory is current.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Local iOS simulator tests are unavailable because this host only has Command Line Tools. The latest GitHub CI report contains no failing or pending checks, including the iOS and macOS Swift lanes.
- Repository autoreview was rerun after the cancellation-aware FIFO and inventory update; no accepted findings remained.
